name: Yota YotaPhone
pros: Wi-Fi support (Wi-Fi 802.11 a/b/g/n, dual-band, hotspot) for data-free browsing and connectivity
1 MP camera capable of capturing good photos for its release era
Snapdragon S4 Pro chipset provides balanced everyday performance
Li-Ion 1800 mAh battery offers solid operating endurance for daily use
cons: No memory card slot -- storage is fixed at purchase
Standard charging speeds without ultra-fast charging support

reviews.title: Solid performance for its 2013 launch era
reviews.body: Picking this up around its release period, the Android 4.2.2 experience felt snappy and responsive for the price tier. The 1 MP camera delivered reliable shots in outdoor lighting.

reviews.title: Reliable battery and daily usability
reviews.body: The Li-Ion 1800 mAh power cell paired with Yota's software tuning easily lasted through a full work day with mixed web browsing, calls, and media playback.

reviews.title: Refined hardware styling and build
reviews.body: The physical chassis of the Yota YotaPhone feels well-balanced in hand. Its 133.6 x 67 x 10 mm (5.26 x 2.64 x 0.39 in) make it easy to hold during long daily sessions.

reviews.title: Great value for the hardware specifications
reviews.body: For the price point, getting Snapdragon S4 Pro performance alongside 32GB storage, no card slot made the Yota YotaPhone an easy recommendation among rivals in 2013.

reviews.title: Smooth day-to-day software responsiveness
reviews.body: Operating on Android 4.2.2, the user interface is intuitive with smooth system transitions. Core apps and browsing run without noticeable stutter.

reviews.title: Dependable display and audio clarity
reviews.body: The screen (Li-Ion 1800 mAh, non-removable, 4.3", 720x1280 pixels) produces vibrant colors for video streaming, and call clarity through the earpiece is crystal clear.

reviews.title: A well-rounded package from Yota
reviews.body: Overall, the Yota YotaPhone proved to be a durable and well-engineered mobile device representing Yota's design philosophy nicely.
